# simdjson / fuzz_atpointer

simdjson's own fuzz target `fuzz_atpointer` ([source](source/fuzz_atpointer.cpp), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over simdjson (simdjson/simdjson at f807de97).

dom::parser::parse of the first split string, then root.at_pointer(second string) and leaf.get_string(); every result is only used to return 0.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against simdjson at commit f807de97 with 1 patch to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- assert(strings.size() >= 2) directly after a loop that pads the vector to two entries: trivially true (the compiler removes it; the assert text is absent from the plain binary) ([lines 19-22](source/fuzz_atpointer.cpp#L19-L22)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch simdjson` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|

| ubsan | `fuzz_atpointer.ubsan` | 461,704 | `4abc9df2c4f94ffea42fd9ad5b47d17e5b47d1079a62c3f1e1bfcd13bc2d1b4c` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
